narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

The day will warm to a high of 30°C (86°F) with a clear sky early, turning mostly cloudy by midday and remaining mostly cloudy into the evening. Thunder possible, peaking this evening, and isolated evening showers and thunderstorms may arrive after 18:00. The wind will be north-northeasterly overnight, shifting to southwest by midday, with gusts reaching 33 km/h (18 kt). UV index peaks at 8.9. Air quality is modeled at AQI 75, though ground stations show a range up to 110 at Dunga Beach. As of 06:01, reports through 03:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 23°C (73°F); low so far 22°C (72°F); peak sustained 7 km/h (4 kt); sky clear.

## Extended Outlook

Next three days will see temperatures and winds much the same through Wednesday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Monday will be partly cloudy, Tuesday partly cloudy, and Wednesday mostly cloudy. Models suggest rain on Monday (2 of 4 models wet) and Tuesday (4 of 4 wet), while Wednesday has 2 of 4 wet with rain amounts ranging up to 32.2 mm (1.27 in). Highs for Day+3 range between 29 and 30°C (86°F). The record notes ECMWF as the best rain caller for Day+3.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Peak CAPE values indicate thunderstorm potential, with the strongest at 19:00. Thunder possible, peaking this evening, could bring sudden gusts well above the forecast wind of 33 km/h (18 kt). No explicit severe weather bulletin from KMD was issued.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Winam Gulf wind will be easterly overnight at 5 km/h (3 kt), gusting 8 km/h (4 kt), then shift to south-southwesterly by midday at 5 km/h (3 kt), gusting 17 km/h (9 kt), and increase to 11 km/h (6 kt) with gusts of 16 km/h (9 kt) into the evening. Peak gust on the gulf is 24 km/h (13 kt). Thunderstorm gusts could exceed these values if thunderstorms develop.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1008 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1016 hPa) – a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Basin pressure today averages between 1013.3 and 1015.5 hPa, with a slight upward trend of +1.0 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

Review finds no model clearly superior for today, though GFS missed the thunderstorm onset and over-forecasted clouds. Best Match under-forecasts both daytime highs and peak wind. ECMWF under-forecasts highs and peak wind, while KMD provides fewer observations for direct comparison. The call aligns with the higher probability from Best Match and ECMWF, but KMD’s own forecast of light showers and thunderstorms matches the overall guidance. Data sufficiency is strong, with 71 checks for the least-covered model, giving a settled picture despite uneven model coverage.
